newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile sees $1.3 bln highway investment in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Chile sees $1.3 bln highway investment in 1997.

text.p: Chile expects investments in road concession projects to climb to $1.3 billion this year from $270 million in 1996, said Public Works Minister Ricardo Lagos.
"We are in the peak moment of the concessions program," Lagos told a news conference.

Investments by private companies this year will be more than the public works ministry's budget for the whole year, which is $900 million, he said. The government's plan includes awarding concessions for six highway projects this year totalling $1.4 billion, said Lagos.
Most of these schemes involve widening the important highway known as Route Five which runs the length of the country but which is just two lanes wide in many places.
The concessions project allows private companies to finance and build highways in exchange for the right to charges tolls on the road for a fixed period.

The system is seen as the only way of funding the massive investments needed to upgrade Chile's antiquated road, rail and port network, which has been overwhelmed by rapid economic growth over the last decade.
